question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund is evaluating whether to launch a Cat III 'Fund-of-Funds' (FoF) that invests across eight external hedge-fund strategies. Based on Section 2.6.1, which statement about hedge-fund FoFs is MOST accurate?

answer.text: FoFs give diversification across strategies but charge SUBSTANTIALLY HIGHER fees, because investors pay management fees at every underlying hedge fund AND an additional layer at the FoF manager level
FoFs charge lower fees than single-strategy hedge funds because management fees are netted off at the top level
FoFs are prohibited under SEBI AIF Regulations from investing in other AIFs
FoFs must invest in exactly one single strategy - multi-strategy at the FoF level is disallowed

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.6.1 explicitly states: "since the investment manager is investing in multiple funds, the fees charged by a FoF are substantially high as compared to single-strategy hedge funds. Fees increase due to management fees charged by every hedge fund and the additional layer of management fees charged by FoF manager." This double-layering is the central trade-off of a FoF: diversification at the cost of fee drag. The Trap: Option B inverts the fee economics - FoFs are MORE expensive, not less. Option C is incorrect because SEBI accommodates FoFs in the AIF space. Option D confuses a FoF with a single-strategy fund wrapper. Note: Pages 40, 47, 112 and 134 of the workbook describe the diversification-versus-fee-drag trade-off; specific fee-stack examples beyond the workbook text should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
